text_blocks.snippet: Central Illinois residents are currently targeted by fraudulent text messages, phone calls, and imposter home service scams demanding immediate payment or personal details. Local authorities and the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois urge residents to stay alert.
snippet_highlighted_words: fraudulent text messages, phone calls, and imposter home service scams demanding immediate payment or personal details

list.snippet: Fake DMV / Toll Texts: Scammers send text messages claiming unpaid tolls, parking fines, or vehicle rebate money, threatening license suspension if you click a link. The State of Illinois never texts about payment.
Imposter Repair Services: Con artists set up fake search engine listings pretending to be real local garage door or HVAC companies, heavily overcharging or sabotaging equipment.
Sheriff / Court Phone Calls: Callers pretend to be local law enforcement or courts claiming you missed a jury duty or court date, demanding payment via Bitcoin or cash to avoid arrest.
Google Listing Verification: Local businesses receive convincing phone calls demanding hundreds of dollars for a "verification fee" to keep search profiles active.
Do not click links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding government fees, tolls, or tickets.

Hang up immediately
if a caller claims to be a sheriff or judge asking for money.
Verify phone numbers independently before hiring repair technicians instead of clicking the top sponsored search result.

Report active threats
or suspicious trends using resources like the BBB Scam Stop Program or the Illinois Attorney General
.
